checks: s < e_min < 1.1547 s for all 9 sizes
d4_max < d2 < s and d2 > thread diameter; d2 == d3 (nominal) in all rows
h2 < h1; all columns non-decreasing with size
no cell disagreement among the sources used (every kept cell: all available sources equal)
shape_hint: A hexagon nut (across flats s, height m) intended to be projection-welded to sheet metal: the weld face carries a short cylindrical centering pilot (diameter d2, height about b) that locates in a hole d3 in the sheet and small weld projections (h1, h2) on the face around it; the thread bore has a chamfer/relief of diameter d4 at the far side.

role_map.d2: centering pilot diameter on the weld face (fits hole d3)
role_map.d3: hole diameter in the sheet for the pilot
role_map.b: standard dimension b (about 0.8-1.5 mm; appears to be the pilot/weld-face height - sources do not describe it)
role_map.h1: standard dimension h1 (weld projection height, 0.55-1.8 mm)
role_map.h2: standard dimension h2 (second projection height, 0.25-1.0 mm)

notes: Only the hexagon DIN 929 was verified (the catalog family also names DIN 928 square, ISO 21670 flange and KS B 1058 - not verified). (M14) is a non-preferred size written in brackets in the standard. The sources give no verbal definition of b, h1, h2 - their roles in role_map are inferred from magnitudes; draftsman should confirm against the standard drawing. DIN 929 is also made in M8x1, M10x1.25 etc. fine pitch and 7/16 UNF - not included. row_support: d4_max and b are supported by exactly 3 sources (digipich, torqbolt, fullerfasteners), h1/h2 by 4, the rest by 4-6.

FE (fasteners.eu-derived): torqbolt.com (table identical to fasteners.eu incl. quirks)
digipich.com (page says: values from single source fasteners.eu)

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched all 6 listed URLs (+fasteners.eu DIN 929) live, all HTTP 200. Parsed with Python; 9 rows x 10 value cols compared per source: fasten.it 54 cells (P,d2,d3,m,s,e_min) 54 ok; lexikon 45 (m,s,d2,h1,h2) 45 ok; boltsfastener 16 (M6-M12 s,e,m,d1) 16 ok; digipich 90 ok; fuller 4 sub-tables 90 ok (fuller d1/d2/d3 re-mapped via tolerance labels d11/H13/max); torqbolt==fasteners.eu table cell-identical. 0 mismatches (lexikon 'e' column is the theoretical 1.1547*s, not e min, correctly ignored). Support per kept column after drops: P 3 (fasten.it, FE, fuller), s 4-5, e_min 3 (fasten.it, FE, fuller; +boltsfastener M6-M12), m 5, d2 5, d3 3 (fasten.it, FE, fuller). Dropped columns: d4_max and b only FE+fuller = 2 clusters; h1/h2 = lexikon+FE+fuller = 3 clusters but role not defined by any source. Physical: s<e_min<1.1547s, d4<d2<s, h2<h1, all monotone.
problems: FE cluster = fasteners.eu + torqbolt + digipich (identical tables / explicit provenance) counts as ONE source: the producer counted digipich and torqbolt as 2 extra independent sources.
b and d4_max have only 2 clusters (FE, fullerfasteners) -> fail T2; dropped.

b, h1, h2: no source text/header defines their physical role (only symbols with nominal/max/min); producer's role_map and Korean labels (projection height etc.) are inferred from magnitude -> dropped per instruction. h1/h2 would otherwise have 3 clusters (lexikon, FE, fuller) and could be restored as bare-symbol columns without role text.
d4_max role (thread-side chamfer/relief) also not described by sources; fuller calls it d3 and fasten.it/lexikon do not list it.
d2 (pilot, d11) and d3 (sheet hole, H13) roles come only from tolerance classes; numerically identical in all rows (d2==d3), fuller uses d1/d2/d3 symbols shifted by one.
M14 is a bracketed non-preferred size '(M14)' in the standard; row label M14 loses the brackets.
e_min/s = 1.087-1.105 (below 1.1547 theoretical) - consistent in all 4 sources, fine but not a geometric across-corners.
Only coarse-pitch rows kept (fine pitches M8x1.. and 7/16-20 UNF omitted) - OK, no mixing.

standard_full: DIN 929 (hexagon weld nuts with projections, 12-2013 table; sizes M3-M16)
